- Certified type: Mechanical multi-jet dry dial water meter type for metering of cold water
- Types: MD-K, MD-K1, MD-KP, MD-KP1

The table on page 2-3 is the key matrix. Let me parse it.

Table structure:
- Type: MD-K / MD-K1 / MD-KP / MD-KP1 (all types)
- Nominal diameter DN: mm → 15 (4 columns), 20 (4 columns)
- Permanent flowrate Q3: m³/h → 2,5 (DN15, 4 cols), 4 (DN20, 4 cols)
- Minimum flowrate Q1: m³/h → 0,03125, 0,025, 0,02, 0,015625 (DN15, R=80,100,125,160), 0,05, 0,04, 0,032, 0,025 (DN20, R=80,100,125,160)
- Transitional flowrate Q2: m³/h → 0,05, 0,04, 0,032, 0,025 (DN15), 0,08, 0,064, 0,0512, 0,04 (DN20)
- Overload flowrate Q4: m³/h → 3,125 (DN15), 5 (DN20)

Second table (page 3):
- Ratio Q3/Q1: R → 80, 100, 125, 160 (DN15), 80, 100, 125, 160 (DN20)
- Ratio Q2/Q1: → 1,6 (all)
- Connection thread: → G ¾ B (DN15), G 1 B (DN20)
- Construction length L: mm → 165/190 (DN15), 190 (DN20)
- Installation orientation: H (all)
- Water temperature range Θ: °C → 0,1 to 50 (T50) — so 0.1 to 50 °C
- Maximum working pressure: bar → 16
- MPE upper range Q2≤Q≤Q4: % → ±2 (at Θ≤30°C), ±3 (at Θ>30°C)
- MPE lower range Q1≤Q<Q2: % → ±5
- Scale interval: m³ → 0,00005
- Indication range: m³ → 9999
- Mechanical class: M1
- Climatic class: °C → -10 to +55
- Electromagnetic class: E1

So this is a model matrix with two axes: DN (15, 20) and ratio R (80, 100, 125, 160). That's 8 model variants:
- DN15, R80: Q3=2.5, Q1=0.03125, Q2=0.05, Q4=3.125
- DN15, R100: Q1=0.025, Q2=0.04
- DN15, R125: Q1=0.02, Q2=0.032
- DN15, R160: Q1=0.015625, Q2=0.025
- DN20, R80: Q3=4, Q1=0.05, Q2=0.08, Q4=5

- DN20, R125: Q1=0.032, Q2=0.0512
- DN20, R160: Q1=0.025, Q2=0.04

Model IDs: I'll use "DN15 R80", "DN15 R100", etc.

Also there are four type designations (MD-K, MD-K1, MD-KP, MD-KP1) which differ by body material (brass vs plastic) and register shape — all share the same metrological table. So the matrix is DN × R, common across all types.
